item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Cordae Hit With $15M Contract Lawsuit That May Derail Anderson .Paak Collab Album
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: MMMG sought millions and an order to stop new releases as it claimed Cordae’s 2018 recording deal remained in force.
item.content:encoded:
Cordae faced a new lawsuit eight days before his joint album with Anderson .Paak was due.

MMMG sued the rapper and three labels on October 15, claiming an old deal gave it control of his new music.

The 20-page complaint obtained by AllHipHop named EMPIRE, Apeshit and Mass Appeal alongside Cordae. It asked a New York federal court to halt releases that MMMG claimed violated its rights.

“Defendants never requested nor received a license from MMMG to release this album,” MMMG’s lawyer, Jeffrey M. Movit of Cohen & Gresser, wrote.

The label based its claims on a deal dated April 2018. It alleged that the deal still bound Cordae to record for MMMG alone.

The suit targeted “A Good Day,” the single and video released on September 16.

It also challenged the rollout of Heavy Is The Crown, set for October 23 through APESHIT + EMPIRE / Hi Level + Mass Appeal.

The fight reached beyond one song. MMMG alleged that Cordae had also kept its share of income from merch, touring and other work.

The company alleged that “he refuses to pay MMMG its contractual share of the revenues.”

The label traced the dispute to a change in how his music reached stores and streaming services.

It said Atlantic ended its deal on September 2, 2025. MMMG claimed it secured a new deal with Stem and told Cordae’s lawyers two days later.

That mattered because the contract allowed a six-month search for a new distributor, according to the suit.

MMMG alleged that its Stem deal kept Cordae’s contract alive. It said his lawyers later disputed whether that deal met the contract’s terms.

The complaint gave MMMG’s account of that exchange. No defense response appeared in the five public docket entries reviewed.

Cordae and Anderson .Paak’s ties stretched back to “RNP” in 2019.

Their song appeared on The Lost Boy, Cordae’s debut through ART@WAR and Atlantic. The new project took that partnership from guest spots to a shared album.

Cordae launched Hi Level in June 2021 while he was still signed to Atlantic. He made ownership a key part of his pitch for the new label.

For “A Good Day,” the suit sought at least $5 million or, as an alternative, damages set by copyright law.

It requested at least $15 million from Cordae for breach of contract. It also sought at least $5 million from the labels for allegedly causing that breach.

MMMG also asked for a jury trial and an order to bar further use of recordings it claimed it owned.

item.title: Cardi B’s Birkin Collection Takes A Hit As Esmeralda Goes Missing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B said her Birkin Esmeralda is missing and thinks she left it in a hotel, calling it the only bag she can't find.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B said she lost the Hermès Birkin she named Esmeralda and thinks she left the purse behind at a hotel.

The rapper shared the news after a fan asked her to bring the bag back out. The request included an older clip of the brown leather purse.

“I fuvkin lost her ….its the only bag missing …I think I left her in a hotel and I’m so sad about it,” she wrote.

She had recently shown off a haul of new purses, including three Birkins she had bought over the span of a few weeks. Esmeralda isn’t the first purse to give her a headache.

In March 2025, she showed fans a mustard-yellow crocodile Birkin that her daughter had marked up. Cardi said that bag had cost her $60,000. She had first shown it off in October 2024 alongside two other new crocodile-skin bags.

Her hunt for rare pieces has taken her overseas before.

During a Vogue shoot at Paris Couture Week in July 2023, Cardi joked that she had really come to buy a Birkin. She said she spent two months looking for one she couldn’t find in the United States.

That collector’s eye became part of a business deal this year. On May 20, Fashionphile named Cardi its 2026 brand ambassador for the “Get Your Bag” campaign, which centered on shopping and reselling pre-owned luxury accessories.

She also curated a selection of her favorites for the platform, with pieces from Hermès, Chanel and Goyard.

Her picks included a crocodile Birkin 25 and a burgundy Chanel tote. The partnership brought her interest in rare finds and classics into the retailer’s shop-and-sell model.

Founder and president Sarah Davis said at the launch that Cardi understood the pieces’ value and could help broaden the audience for luxury resale.

Cardi pointed to its range of rare bags and classic styles, along with authenticity, as reasons the partnership made sense for her as a collector.

In her launch statement, Cardi summed up her taste: “I love a good bag, but I love a smart buy too.”

item.title: Police Find No Lil Baby Link To Keion White Shooting Suspects
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Police found no link between Lil Baby and Keion White's shooting suspects as one man was ordered released and another stayed jailed.
item.content:encoded:
Police have found no connection between Lil Baby and the suspects in Keion White’s shooting case, even as the nightclub attack moved into court.

KQED reported that finding after Gregory Walker and Curtis Green appeared at San Francisco’s Hall of Justice on Wednesday, October 14. A judge ordered Green released on misdemeanor gun charges, while Walker remained jailed without bail on felony counts.

The two men postponed entering pleas and were due back for arraignment Monday, October 19. The judge ordered both not to possess weapons.

Walker’s attorney, Jeff Wozniak, disputed the case against his client and said he would seek his release.

“We’re gonna show that he’s innocent, get him back to his family,” Wozniak said.

The court decisions added a new step after officials announced four arrests in the investigation. Police described a broader operation involving more than 50 search warrants and help from more than 250 law enforcement personnel.

White was hosting a private Super Bowl party downstairs at Dahlia’s in San Francisco when he was shot in the ankle early February 9.

The San Francisco Standard reviewed a police report in which a witness said Lil Baby’s entourage tried to enter White’s event.

The witness described an argument between White and the rapper, then heard gunfire while upstairs asking club managers for help. He told police he did not know who shot White.

Prosecutors alleged Walker and a second man awaiting charges fired guns, wounding the 49ers defensive lineman.

The district attorney’s office charged Walker with assault with a semiautomatic firearm and three felony gun-possession counts. It also alleged he personally fired a gun and caused great bodily injury.

Green’s charges were different. Prosecutors accused him of brandishing a firearm, carrying a concealed firearm and carrying a loaded firearm in public, all misdemeanors.

Authorities arrested Green in Irvine on October 7 and Walker in Los Angeles on October 9. Both were booked into San Francisco County Jail on October 12.

Police also identified Marquis Davis and Antoine Washington as suspects. Officials were still arranging their transfer to San Francisco when the court report was published.

The investigation remained open, with Walker and Green’s next court appearance set for Monday.

item.title: Kevin Hart Lands Fox Deal To Turn Short Dramas Into Films & TV
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kevin Hart's Hartbeat secured a Fox partnership built around 25 short dramas, adding a new route to film and television.
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Hart struck a new deal with Fox Entertainment that could turn phone-screen dramas from his Hartbeat company into films and full-length TV shows.

The lineup starts with 25 live-action shows, with thrillers, dramas and faith-based plots. They’ll debut on a Codeblack channel in My Drama, the video app run by Holywater Tech, under the Codeblack, Essence and Revolt brands.

Fox’s studio got the first chance to develop them into films and longer TV shows. Its global arm will sell the shorts abroad once their first runs on the app end.

The goal is to see what draws fans before making longer shows. The three brands have more than 20 million combined social followers, the companies said.

“Hartbeat has a powerful creative voice and an exceptional instinct for stories that connect with audiences,” Fox scripted chief Hannah Pillemer said in the deal announcement.

The move followed Hart’s defense of cuts at Hartbeat in May. Speaking on “The Breakfast Club,” he said his business had grown too large and needed to cut costs.

“My company was too big. I don’t need 80 people to operate how we’re operating now,” he said. “Downsize. Save the money.”

Hart said the cuts were meant to keep the business running well while he kept making films and shows through his own team. He pushed back at the idea that a smaller staff meant the end of Hartbeat.

In January, Hart took a stake in Authentic Brands Group as part of a deal to jointly own and run the Kevin Hart brand. The partners laid out plans to put his name on more products, digital ventures and live events.

His ties to Fox also predate this latest pact. Fox-owned Tubi announced a four-film Hartbeat deal in October 2025, built around stars who had already drawn fans online.

That deal included “Sundown,” written and directed by Kinigra Deon, who also starred, and “85 South: Dead End,” featuring DC Young Fly, Chico Bean and Karlous Miller. The two firms had worked together before, bringing Hartbeat films and shows to the free streaming service.

Hartbeat also struck a deal with aTwist in September for more than 20 original short shows. That slate included LOL comedies and plans to turn Blake Karrington’s books into series with Upscale Productions. Hartbeat could draw on fans of those books as it sought an audience for its new shows.

The Fox deal’s value was not disclosed. No films or full-length TV shows were named.

item.title: Tajai Of Hieroglyphics Seeks $500K To Rebuild Panama Hotel After Earthquake
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Tajai sought $500,000 to rebuild his earthquake-damaged Panama hotel, with aid for 10 workers at the heart of the appeal.
item.content:encoded:
Tajai asked fans to help rebuild his Panama hotel after an earthquake left parts of it in ruins. The Hieroglyphics MC’s $500,000 appeal prioritizes aid for his staff.

The first $40,000 would help Hotel Hibiscus Garden’s 10 workers and their families get through six months without steady work. The rest would help rebuild the hotel, restaurant and a planned community gym.

“We are safe, and we are grateful for that,” the campaign stated.

It described cracked rooms and a wrecked workshop. “The restaurant’s entire second floor has been destroyed and is in danger of collapse.”

Most buildings may need to come down, though engineers still need to check them. The campaign’s $500,000 goal could change once those checks and building bids are in.

Panama declared a state of emergency after the October 9 quake damaged homes, schools, roads and health centers. Veraguas, where the hotel is based, was among the areas the government singled out for aid.

For Tajai, the damage hit a project he had spent a decade building. The Pacific coast hotel near Santa Catalina also operates as Bliss Beach Panama, a place for artists and travelers to unwind. Before the quake, guests could take yoga classes or join group retreats.

A volunteer exchange program also let visitors stay longer and help out.

Tajai’s roots in Hip-Hop go back much further. The Oakland MC formed Souls of Mischief with A-Plus, Opio and Phesto in high school. The four joined the wider Hieroglyphics crew with Del The Funky Homosapien, Casual and Pep Love.

Their 1993 debut, 93 ‘Til Infinity, offered a fresh take on West Coast rap. The group’s sharp rhymes and laid-back beats set them apart from much of that era’s gangsta rap. The title track reached No. 72 on the Hot 100, giving the group its first chart hit.

He also helped run Hieroglyphics’ business. The crew built an artist-owned label and stayed close to fans as it forged a life outside the major-label system. Souls of Mischief celebrated 30 years since their 2023 debut with a 93-date world tour.

Tajai brought a second set of skills to his Panama venture.

Alongside his rap career, he trained in building design and earned a master’s in architecture from the University of California, Berkeley. His hotel grew into a space for visiting artists and local events.

The campaign promised spending updates every two weeks. Readers can support the Hotel Hibiscus Garden rebuilding fundraiser here.

item.title: Black Girls Rock! Plans “BGR! LIVE” Arena Tour For 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Black Girls Rock! and Black Promoters Collective announced "BGR! LIVE," with a national arena tour planned for early 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Black Girls Rock! and Black Promoters Collective announced a multiyear partnership on October 14 to launch “BGR! LIVE,” a concert platform with a U.S. arena tour planned for early 2027.

The partners said the platform would also encompass concerts and festivals.

Black Girls Rock! has used its awards to honor Black women across music, art and public life. The partners said the tour would reach select U.S. cities, though they did not name the cities, artists, venues or ticket dates.

“I’m thrilled to launch BGR! LIVE with Black Promoters Collective, an exceptional team of industry leaders with a proven track record of delivering world-class tours,” Black Girls Rock! founder Beverly Bond said in the announcement. “Our partnership combines that expertise with the audience connection and cultural identity that make BLACK GIRLS ROCK! distinctive. Together, we’re opening a new era for the brand, bringing our creative vision and cultural impact to the grandest stages through extraordinary experiences that celebrate Black music, artistry, and community.”

Bond founded Black Girls Rock! in 2006. What began as a way to spotlight Black women’s achievements grew into awards, arts education and mentorship.

In a 2010 Black Enterprise interview, Bond recalled that a T-shirt listing women she admired became the seed for a mentoring program. She also described DJ lessons as a way for girls to build discipline and creative skills.

The awards reached BET in 2010, taking Bond’s work to a national TV audience.

Black Promoters Collective brings experience with large R&B and Hip-Hop tours. In a June Pollstar interview, CEO Gary Guidry said the company had passed $100 million in top-line revenue in 2025.

He described concert formats that put major acts in a shared show rather than a standard opener-and-headliner setup.

“Our investment in BGR! LIVE reflects our conviction that BLACK GIRLS ROCK! can command a major place in national touring,” Guidry said in the new announcement. “Beverly Bond has built an institution with enduring cultural authority that has helped define how Black women are celebrated. We are committed to building a lasting business together and delivering live experiences that set a high standard for the industry.”

item.title: Diddy’s “Dudus” Prison Fight Story Hit With Flat Denial
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Sources close to Dudus denied Diddy's alleged prison fight, saying the men had never crossed paths at the New Jersey facility.
item.content:encoded:
Diddy’s alleged prison fight with Christopher “Dudus” Coke was denied by sources close to the former Jamaican crime boss.

Nationwide Radio Jamaica reported Thursday that its newsroom spoke with those sources on Wednesday evening, October 14.

They told the station that Dudus had never crossed paths with Diddy at the New Jersey prison.

The broadcaster did not name those sources. It said their account led it to change its first report about the alleged clash.

“Based on the information from our highly placed sources, we moved to amend our original reporting on the matter,” the station wrote.

The denial followed several reports offering different explanations for Diddy’s head injury.

On October 12, a representative told Us Weekly, “We are aware of the reports concerning Sean Combs and are working to confirm the circumstances.”

The prison told that outlet separately that it would not discuss an individual’s housing or medical status, citing privacy, safety and security.

A bunk-bed explanation emerged October 13. An unnamed source told Page Six that Diddy hit his head on the bunk above him. That report did not name Dudus as the cause.

An October 14 TMZ report alleged the two men fought at Fort Dix, linking the encounter to Diddy’s head injury.

Diddy’s former bodyguard Roger Bonds offered another version Thursday.

Bonds claimed his own sources inside Fort Dix described a minor skirmish between the two men. He said Diddy was not struck in the head and that the men went their separate ways.

Bonds’ account still described a confrontation.

The station’s sources close to Dudus disputed any encounter between them.

Dudus led the Shower Posse, also known as the Presidential Click, before receiving a 23-year federal sentence in June 2012.

He pleaded guilty to racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to commit assault with a dangerous weapon in aid of racketeering.

Federal prosecutors described a network with members in Jamaica and the United States. Its drug business reached New York and Miami, with profits and U.S.-bought guns sent to Dudus in Jamaica.

Diddy is serving a 50-month term following his federal trial.

Jurors convicted him of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution and acquitted him of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking.

item.title: Floyd Mayweather Fawns Over Donald Trump Onstage At Midterm Rally
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Floyd Mayweather joined Donald Trump in Arizona as the president rallied support for Republican candidates ahead of Election Day.
item.content:encoded:
Floyd Mayweather backed President Donald Trump onstage at an Arizona rally on Wednesday, October 14, adding his voice to the president’s push for Republican wins in next month’s midterm elections.

The boxer joined Trump at Laughlin/Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City. He flew from Las Vegas with the president aboard Air Force One.

Trump introduced Mayweather by praising his defense and linking that style to the boxer’s looks. He also highlighted Mayweather’s earnings before inviting him to the microphone. He referred to the boxer by his “Money” nickname.

“He looks so good. Who would believe he’s a fighter? He looks so good. He doesn’t have a mark, that’s why I’d rather be a great defensive fighter,” President Trump gushed.

Mayweather then said, “we couldn’t have chose a better president twice than Donald Trump.”

He thanked those who came out, praised the United States and recalled representing the country at the 1996 Olympic Games.

“America is the best country in the world. If I died and came back a million times, I will always choose America. We couldn’t have chose a better president twice than Donald Trump. So, it’s all about keeping this country strong, and it’s all about us sticking together and believing one another. America is the best country in the world,” Floyd Mayweather told the crowd.

He ended his brief remarks by urging Americans to stick together and believe in one another.

Afterward, Trump thanked Mayweather and dwelled on his unbeaten 50-0 record, noting that he had faced top opponents throughout his boxing career.

Combat sports outlet Happy Punch shared a clip of his remarks that evening.

Mayweather also appeared at the Republican Jewish Coalition’s 2025 leadership summit in Las Vegas. He accepted its World Champion for Israel Award and spoke about his support for Israel.

Mayweather had voiced his support for Trump well before this campaign stop. He also attended Trump’s first presidential inauguration in January 2017.

During a February 2025 appearance on Fox Business’s “Making Money with Charles Payne,” he praised Trump’s work as president and his business background.

AllHipHop reported at the time that 50 Cent mocked the interview in an Instagram post.

“LOL YO you know how, when you’re in school and a kid eats the crayons,” 50 Cent wrote in the caption. “Now you see what happens when they grow up. Spell BEST PRESIDENT champ! LOL.”

The Arizona stop placed him alongside a recent string of boxers who joined Trump on the road. Mike Tyson appeared at a rally on October 9 in Syracuse, New York.

Jake Paul joined an October 12 event in Youngstown, Ohio. Mayweather’s appearance made three boxers at three Trump rallies in six days.

In Bullhead City, Trump sought votes for U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs, the Republican challenging Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs. Biggs took the stage and urged the crowd to support Republicans throughout the ticket.

The visit came while early voting was underway in Arizona. Races for governor, attorney general and the U.S. House were on the November 3 ballot.

item.title: Eminem Stays On Kid Rock Album As Lil Wayne Takes Over “7 Sins”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Eminem remained on Kid Rock's gospel album as Lil Wayne took over "7 Sins" and the Detroit rapper moved to "Heal My Faith."
item.content:encoded:
Eminem kept his spot on Kid Rock’s gospel album as Lil Wayne took over “7 Sins,” the song at the center of a clash over the Detroit stars’ politics.

Kid Rock shared the change on October 14, then posted a new tracklist for Halfway 2 Jesus. The image listed Lil Wayne on the third song, “7 Sins,” and Eminem on the fifth, “Heal My Faith.”

Kid Rock used a new video to address fans who didn’t want him to work with Eminem. He first teased that those critics might be glad to hear Eminem was off “7 Sins.”

He then named Lil Wayne as the new guest before sharing the other half of the news

“Eminem is still on the album. He’s just on another song now, called ‘Heal My Faith,'” Kid Rock said.

Kid Rock’s ties to Eminem went back long before this record. AllHipHop’s earlier report noted Eminem’s guest spot on “F#ck Off” from Kid Rock’s 1998 album Devil Without A Cause. Kid Rock later appeared in Eminem’s “Berzerk” video.

The first look at “7 Sins” had brought that friendship into a fresh debate.

On October 5, critics criticized Eminem’s choice to work with Kid Rock, who backed Donald Trump. Eminem had appeared at a Kamala Harris campaign rally in Detroit in 2024, putting the pair on opposite sides of that race.

Kid Rock told Fox News earlier this month that he and Eminem had agreed to keep politics from dividing their friendship.

In the new video, Kid Rock again stood by his choice to work with people who held different views.

He said the guests, musicians, songwriters and engineers who made the album did not all think alike. He framed that right to hold different views as part of what made the country great.

Halfway 2 Jesus was scheduled to arrive on October 17, the date in Kid Rock’s X announcement.

item.title: Lord Conrad Drops Highly Anticipated Single “Rising Empire”
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Lord Conrad blends 80s synthwave, hip-hop, trap, and heavy 808s on “Rising Empire,” a GTA 6-inspired release fueled by Vice City nightlife, luxury, ambition, and cinematic gaming culture.
item.content:encoded:
Neon nights. Luxury cars. Champagne. Heavy 808s. The rise of an empire.

Enter a world of 80s synthwave, distorted electric guitars, modern hip-hop, and trap, where retro neon aesthetics collide with luxury, ambition, and the streets of Vice City.

Rising Empire is a GTA 6-inspired musical experience by Lord Conrad, capturing the energy of Vice City, cinematic open-world gaming, neon nightlife, and the rise of a new generation.

From the neon streets of GTA6 to the real-world financial markets, the empire-building mindset goes beyond the game.

With the gaming industry evolving and the spotlight on the future of Grand Theft Auto VI, the market keeps its eyes on Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ: TTWO), the company behind the Grand Theft Auto franchise, alongside the broader Nasdaq and the business of interactive entertainment.

Ambition. Innovation. Risk. The next big move.

Rising Empire — where gaming culture, financial ambition, and music collide.

THE RISING EMPIRE EXPERIENCE

GTA 6 / GTA VI Inspired

Vice City & Neon Nights

Luxury Cars & Midnight Drives

Champagne & Luxury Lifestyle

80s Synthwave & Distorted Guitars

Modern Hip-Hop, Trap & Heavy 808s

This is more than a vibe. It’s a statement.

Lord Conrad is rising. The empire starts now.
